claim: The extension-free Echo client can connect, read, mutate once, deduplicate a repeated operation ID, and stop in a real cmux WebKit tab.
observations: A human-triggered Connect action changed visible state to Agent access active.
readState returned success through the MCP endpoint.
setDraft with operation ID webkit-local-2 changed the independently read textarea value to Updated by local WebKit.
A second setDraft with the same operation ID and different text returned the prior success receipt; the textarea remained Updated by local WebKit.
The human-only Stop button changed visible state to Agent access stopped.
A call after Stop returned session_closed and did not change the textarea.
limitations: cmux WKWebView is WebKit evidence but is not a named Safari run.
The test used a loopback development Worker rather than a remote deployment.
The first two attempts exposed Worker authorization and readonly-state ordering defects; this receipt describes the corrected run only.
